featuresBackground.name: Folk Hero
featuresBackground.description:
You come from a humble social rank, but you are destined for so much more. Already the people of your home village regard you as their champion, and your destiny calls you to stand against the tyrants and monsters that threaten the common folk everywhere.

 
Skill Proficiencies: Animal Handling, Survival
Tool Proficiencies: One type of artisan’s tools, vehicles (land)
Equipment: A set of artisan’s tools (one of your choice), a shovel, an iron pot, a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 10 gp
 
Defining Event

You previously pursued a simple profession among the peasantry, perhaps as a farmer, miner, servant, shepherd, woodcutter, or gravedigger. But something happened that set you on a different path and marked you for greater things. Choose or randomly determine a defining event that marked you as a hero of the people.

d10 Defining Event
1 I stood up to a tyrant’s agents.
2 I saved people during a natural disaster.
3 I stood alone against a terrible monster.
4 I stole from a corrupt merchant to help the poor.
5 I led a militia to fight off an invading army.
6 I broke into a tyrant’s castle and stole weapons to arm the people.
7 I trained the peasantry to use farm implements as weapons against a tyrant’s soldiers.
8 A lord rescinded an unpopular decree after I led a symbolic act of protest against it.
9 A celestial, fey, or similar creature gave me a blessing or revealed my secret origin.
10 Recruited into a lord’s army, I rose to leadership and was commended for my heroism.

FEATURE: RUSTIC HOSPITALITY

Since you come from the ranks of the common folk, you fit in among them with ease. You can find a place to hide, rest, or recuperate among other commoners, unless you have shown yourself to be a danger to them. They will shield you from the law or anyone else searching for you, though they will not risk their lives for you.

 
Suggested Characteristics

A folk hero is one of the common people, for better or for worse. Most folk heroes look on their humble origins as a virtue, not a shortcoming, and their home communities remain very important to them.

d8 Personality Trait
1 I judge people by their actions, not their words.
2 If someone is in trouble, I’m always ready to lend help.
3 When I set my mind to something, I follow through no matter what gets in my way.
4 I have a strong sense of fair play and always try to find the most equitable solution to arguments.
5 I’m confident in my own abilities and do what I can to instill confidence in others.
6 Thinking is for other people. I prefer action.
7 I misuse long words in an attempt to sound smarter.
8 I get bored easily. When am I going to get on with my destiny?
d6 Ideal
1 Respect. People deserve to be treated with dignity and respect. (Good)
2 Fairness. No one should get preferential treatment before the law, and no one is above the law. (Lawful)
3 Freedom. Tyrants must not be allowed to oppress the people. (Chaotic)
4 Might. If I become strong, I can take what I want—what I deserve. (Evil)
5 Sincerity. There’s no good in pretending to be something I’m not. (Neutral)
6 Destiny. Nothing and no one can steer me away from my higher calling. (Any)
d6 Bond
1 I have a family, but I have no idea where they are. One day, I hope to see them again.
2 I worked the land, I love the land, and I will protect the land.
3 A proud noble once gave me a horrible beating, and I will take my revenge on any bully I encounter.
4 My tools are symbols of my past life, and I carry them so that I will never forget my roots.
5 I protect those who cannot protect themselves.
6 I wish my childhood sweetheart had come with me to pursue my destiny.
d6 Flaw
1 The tyrant who rules my land will stop at nothing to see me killed.
2 I’m convinced of the significance of my destiny, and blind to my shortcomings and the risk of failure.
3 The people who knew me when I was young know my shameful secret, so I can never go home again.
4 I have a weakness for the vices of the city, especially hard drink.
5 Secretly, I believe that things would be better if I were a tyrant lording over the land.
6 I have trouble trusting in my allies.

Found throughout the multiverse, humans are as varied as they are numerous.

Human Traits
Resourceful, Skillful, Versatile
race.longDescription:
Found throughout the multiverse, humans are as varied as they are numerous, and they endeavor to achieve as much as they can in the years they are given. Their ambition and resourcefulness are commended, respected, and feared on many worlds.

Humans are as diverse in appearance as the people of Earth, and they have many gods. Scholars dispute the origin of humanity, but one of the earliest known human gatherings is said to have occurred in Sigil, the torus-shaped city at the center of the multiverse and the place where the Common language was born. From there, humans could have spread to every part of the multiverse, bringing the City of Doors’ cosmopolitanism with them.

Your character knows at least three languages: Common plus two languages you roll or choose from the Standard Languages table. Knowledge of a language means your character can communicate in it, read it, and write it. Your class and other features might also give you languages.

The Standard Languages table lists languages that are widespread on D&D worlds. Every player character knows Common, which originated in the planar metropolis of Sigil, the hub of the multiverse. The other standard languages originated with the first members of the most prominent species in the worlds of D&D and have since spread widely.

definition.name: Barbarian
definition.description:
A Fierce Warrior of Primal Rage

Barbarians are mighty warriors who are powered by primal forces of the multiverse that manifest as a Rage.

Primary Ability: Strength
Hit Point Die: D12
Saves: Strength & Constitution
definition.equipmentDescription:
Choose A or B:
(A) Greataxe, 4 Handaxes, Explorer’s Pack, and 15 GP; or
(B) 75 GP

classFeatures.name: Rage
classFeatures.description:
You can imbue yourself with a primal power called Rage, a force that grants you extraordinary might and resilience. You can enter it as a Bonus Action if you aren’t wearing Heavy armor.

You can enter your Rage the number of times shown for your Barbarian level in the Rages column of the Barbarian Features table. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

While active, your Rage follows the rules below.

Damage Resistance. You have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

Rage Damage. When you make an attack using Strength—with either a weapon or an Unarmed Strike—and deal damage to the target, you gain a bonus to the damage that increases as you gain levels as a Barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian Features table.

Strength Advantage. You have Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.

No Concentration or Spells. You can’t maintain Concentration, and you can’t cast spells.

Duration. The Rage lasts until the end of your next turn, and it ends early if you don Heavy armor or have the Incapacitated condition. If your Rage is still active on your next turn, you can extend the Rage for another round by doing one of the following:

  • Make an attack roll against an enemy.
  • Force an enemy to make a saving throw.
  • Take a Bonus Action to extend your Rage.

Each time the Rage is extended, it lasts until the end of your next turn. You can maintain a Rage for up to 10 minutes.
classFeatures.summary: Gain extraordinary might and resilience for a short time.

classFeatures.name: Unarmored Defense
classFeatures.description: While you aren’t wearing any armor, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Constitution modifiers. You can use a Shield and still gain this benefit.
classFeatures.summary: Improve your base Armor Class when you aren't wearing any armor.

classFeatures.name: Weapon Mastery
classFeatures.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of Simple or Martial Melee weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.

When you reach certain Barbarian levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Barbarian Features table.
classFeatures.summary: Unlock the mastery properties of your chosen weapons.

classFeatures.name: Danger Sense
classFeatures.description: You gain an uncanny sense of when things aren’t as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge perils. You have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws unless you have the Incapacitated condition.

classFeatures.name: Reckless Attack
classFeatures.description: You can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with increased ferocity. When you make your first attack roll on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you Advantage on attack rolls using Strength until the start of your next turn, but attack rolls against you have Advantage during that time.

classFeatures.name: Barbarian Subclass
classFeatures.description: You gain a Barbarian subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Barbarian levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass’s features that are of your Barbarian level or lower.

classFeatures.name: Primal Knowledge
classFeatures.description:
You gain proficiency in another skill of your choice from the skill list available to Barbarians at level 1.

In addition, while your Rage is active, you can channel primal power when you attempt certain tasks; whenever you make an ability check using one of the following skills, you can make it as a Strength check even if it normally uses a different ability: Acrobatics, Intimidation, Perception, Stealth, or Survival. When you use this ability, your Strength represents primal power coursing through you, honing your agility, bearing, and senses.

classFeatures.name: Ability Score Improvement
classFeatures.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Barbarian levels 8, 12, and 16.

classFeatures.name: Extra Attack
classFeatures.description: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

classFeatures.name: Fast Movement
classFeatures.description: Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren’t wearing Heavy armor.

classFeatures.name: Feral Instinct
classFeatures.description: Your instincts are so honed that you have Advantage on Initiative rolls.

classFeatures.name: Instinctive Pounce
classFeatures.description: As part of the Bonus Action you take to enter your Rage, you can move up to half your Speed.

classFeatures.name: 8: Ability Score Improvement
classFeatures.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Barbarian levels 12 and 16.

classFeatures.name: Brutal Strike
classFeatures.description:
If you use Reckless Attack, you can forgo any Advantage on one Strength-based attack roll of your choice on your turn. The chosen attack roll mustn’t have Disadvantage. If the chosen attack roll hits, the target takes an extra 1d10 damage of the same type dealt by the weapon or Unarmed Strike, and you can cause one Brutal Strike effect of your choice. You have the following effect options.

Forceful Blow. The target is pushed 15 feet straight away from you. You can then move up to half your Speed straight toward the target without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

Hamstring Blow. The target’s Speed is reduced by 15 feet until the start of your next turn. A target can be affected by only one Hamstring Blow at a time—the most recent one.

classFeatures.name: Relentless Rage
classFeatures.description:
Your Rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 Hit Points while your Rage is active and don’t die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, your Hit Points instead change to a number equal to twice your Barbarian level.

Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a Short or Long Rest, the DC resets to 10.

classFeatures.name: 12: Ability Score Improvement
classFeatures.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Barbarian level 16.

classFeatures.name: Improved Brutal Strike
classFeatures.description:
You have honed new ways to attack furiously. The following effects are now among your Brutal Strike options.

Staggering Blow. The target has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes, and it can’t make Opportunity Attacks until the start of your next turn.

Sundering Blow. Before the start of your next turn, the next attack roll made by another creature against the target gains a +5 bonus to the roll. An attack roll can gain only one Sundering Blow bonus.

classFeatures.name: Persistent Rage
classFeatures.description:
When you roll Initiative, you can regain all expended uses of Rage. After you regain uses of Rage in this way, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

In addition, your Rage is so fierce that it now lasts for 10 minutes without you needing to do anything to extend it from round to round. Your Rage ends early if you have the Unconscious condition (not just the Incapacitated condition) or don Heavy armor.

classFeatures.name: 16: Ability Score Improvement
classFeatures.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeatures.name: Improved Brutal Strike
classFeatures.description: The extra damage of your Brutal Strike increases to 2d10. In addition, you can use two different Brutal Strike effects whenever you use your Brutal Strike feature.

classFeatures.name: Indomitable Might
classFeatures.description: If your total for a Strength check or Strength saving throw is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.

classFeatures.name: Epic Boon
classFeatures.description: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeatures.name: Primal Champion
classFeatures.description: You embody primal power. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4, and their maximum is now 25.

classFeatures.name: Core Barbarian Traits
classFeatures.description:
As a Level 1 Character:

  • Gain all the traits in the Core Barbarian Traits table.
  • Gain the Barbarian’s level 1 features.
Core Barbarian Traits
Primary Ability Strength
Hit Point Die D12 per Barbarian level
Saving Throw Proficiencies Strength and Constitution
Skill Proficiencies Choose 2: Animal Handling, Athletics, Intimidation, Nature, Perception, or Survival
Weapon Proficiencies Simple and Martial weapons
Armor Training Light and Medium armor and Shields
Starting Equipment Choose A or B: (A) Greataxe, 4 Handaxes, Explorer’s Pack, and 15 GP; or (B) 75 GP

When you reach certain Barbarian levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Barbarian Features table.

classFeatures.description: Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of another kind of Simple or Martial Melee weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of your chosen weapon choices.

  • Channel primal forces to fuel uncanny reflexes and heightened senses.
  • Fight with reckless abandon.

subclassDefinition.name: Path of the Zealot
subclassDefinition.description:
Rage in Ecstatic Union with a God

Barbarians who walk the Path of the Zealot receive boons from a god or pantheon. These Barbarians experience their Rage as an ecstatic episode of divine union that infuses them with power. They are often allies to the priests and other followers of their god or pantheon.

classFeatures.name: Warrior of the Gods
classFeatures.description:
A divine entity helps ensure you can continue the fight. You have a pool of four d12s that you can spend to heal yourself. As a Bonus Action, you can expend dice from the pool, roll them, and regain a number of Hit Points equal to the roll’s total.

Your pool regains all expended dice when you finish a Long Rest.

The pool’s maximum number of dice increases by one when you reach Barbarian levels 6 (5 dice), 12 (6 dice), and 17 (7 dice).

classFeatures.name: Fanatical Focus
classFeatures.description: Once per active Rage, if you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it with a bonus equal to your Rage Damage bonus, and you must use the new roll.

classFeatures.name: Zealous Presence
classFeatures.description:
As a Bonus Action, you unleash a battle cry infused with divine energy. Up to ten other creatures of your choice within 60 feet of you gain Advantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the start of your next turn.

Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest unless you expend a use of your Rage (no action required) to restore your use of it.

classFeatures.name: Rage of the Gods
classFeatures.description:
When you activate your Rage, you can assume the form of a divine warrior. This form lasts for 1 minute or until you drop to 0 Hit Points. Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

While in this form, you gain the benefits below.

Flight. You have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed and can hover.

Resistance. You have Resistance to Necrotic, Psychic, and Radiant damage.

Revivification. When a creature within 30 feet of you would drop to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to expend a use of your Rage to instead change the target’s Hit Points to a number equal to your Barbarian level.

classFeatures.name: Divine Fury
classFeatures.description: You can channel divine power into your strikes. On each of your turns while your Rage is active, the first creature you hit with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike takes extra damage equal to 1d6 plus half your Barbarian level (round down). The extra damage is Necrotic or Radiant; you choose the type each time you deal the damage.

classFeatures.name: Rage
classFeatures.description:
You can imbue yourself with a primal power called Rage, a force that grants you extraordinary might and resilience. You can enter it as a Bonus Action if you aren’t wearing Heavy armor.

You can enter your Rage the number of times shown for your Barbarian level in the Rages column of the Barbarian Features table. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

While active, your Rage follows the rules below.

Damage Resistance. You have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

Rage Damage. When you make an attack using Strength—with either a weapon or an Unarmed Strike—and deal damage to the target, you gain a bonus to the damage that increases as you gain levels as a Barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian Features table.

Strength Advantage. You have Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.

No Concentration or Spells. You can’t maintain Concentration, and you can’t cast spells.

Duration. The Rage lasts until the end of your next turn, and it ends early if you don Heavy armor or have the Incapacitated condition. If your Rage is still active on your next turn, you can extend the Rage for another round by doing one of the following:

  • Make an attack roll against an enemy.
  • Force an enemy to make a saving throw.
  • Take a Bonus Action to extend your Rage.

Each time the Rage is extended, it lasts until the end of your next turn. You can maintain a Rage for up to 10 minutes.

When you reach certain Barbarian levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Barbarian Features table.

classFeatures.name: Danger Sense
classFeatures.description: You gain an uncanny sense of when things aren’t as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge perils. You have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws unless you have the Incapacitated condition.

classFeatures.name: Reckless Attack
classFeatures.description: You can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with increased ferocity. When you make your first attack roll on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you Advantage on attack rolls using Strength until the start of your next turn, but attack rolls against you have Advantage during that time.

When you use this ability, your Strength represents primal power coursing through you, honing your agility, bearing, and senses.

classFeatures.name: Instinctive Pounce

classFeatures.name: 8: Ability Score Improvement

classFeatures.name: Brutal Strike
classFeatures.description:
If you use Reckless Attack, you can forgo any Advantage on one Strength-based attack roll of your choice on your turn. The chosen attack roll mustn’t have Disadvantage. If the chosen attack roll hits, the target takes an extra 1d10 damage of the same type dealt by the weapon or Unarmed Strike, and you can cause one Brutal Strike effect of your choice. You have the following effect options.

Forceful Blow. The target is pushed 15 feet straight away from you. You can then move up to half your Speed straight toward the target without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

Hamstring Blow. The target’s Speed is reduced by 15 feet until the start of your next turn. A target can be affected by only one Hamstring Blow at a time—the most recent one.

classFeatures.name: Relentless Rage
classFeatures.description:
Your Rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 Hit Points while your Rage is active and don’t die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, your Hit Points instead change to a number equal to twice your Barbarian level.

Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a Short or Long Rest, the DC resets to 10.

classFeatures.name: 12: Ability Score Improvement

When you roll Initiative, you can regain all expended uses of Rage. After you regain uses of Rage in this way, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

In addition, your Rage is so fierce that it now lasts for 10 minutes without you needing to do anything to extend it from round to round. Your Rage ends early if you have the Unconscious condition (not just the Incapacitated condition) or don Heavy armor.

definition.description:
A divine entity helps ensure you can continue the fight. You have a pool of four d12s that you can spend to heal yourself. As a Bonus Action, you can expend dice from the pool, roll them, and regain a number of Hit Points equal to the roll’s total.

Your pool regains all expended dice when you finish a Long Rest.

The pool’s maximum number of dice increases by one when you reach Barbarian levels 6 (5 dice), 12 (6 dice), and 17 (7 dice).

Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest unless you expend a use of your Rage (no action required) to restore your use of it.

definition.name: Neutral Faction Renown
definition.description:
Azeroth is defined by its factions— nations, organizations, cartels, and pacts that claim members from around the world. As characters interact with these factions, they can build a reputation and earn tangible and intangible rewards.

This system builds on the renown rules found in the Dungeon Master’s Guide to track characters’ standing with the major factions of Azeroth. In addition, characters might gain renown with smaller groups to achieve short-term goals. World of Warcraft offers abundant examples that can be adapted into a tabletop campaign. For example, characters seeking a route from Felwood into Winterspring might work to gain renown with the furbolgs of Timbermaw Hold, who will allow passage through their tunnels once at least one member of the party has achieved a Renown Score of 10+.

definition.name: Subfaction Renown
definition.description:
The Horde and Alliance are made up of members of many different species, and the most prominent among those species are the subfactions of the Horde and Alliance. Most of these subfactions are named for their capital city, as shown on the list below. The species descriptions in chapter 2 provide more information about these subfactions.

Horde Subfactions Alliance Subfactions
Bilgewater Cartel (goblins) Darnassus (night elves)
Dark Talons (dracthyr) Exodar (draenei)
Darkspear Tribe (trolls) Gilneas (worgen)
Huojin (pandaren) Gnomeregan (gnomes)
Orgrimmar (orcs and vulpera) Ironforge (dwarves)
Silvermoon City (blood elves) Obsidian Warders (dracthyr)
Thunder Bluff (tauren) Stormwind (humans)
Undercity (Forsaken) Tushui (pandaren)

If your species gives you a starting Renown Score with a Horde or Alliance subfaction, gaining renown with different Horde or Alliance subfactions also increases your Renown Score with your starting faction as described below:

Friendly. The first time your Renown Score with each Horde or Alliance faction other than your starting faction reaches 3, increase your Renown Score with your starting faction by 1.
Honored. The first time your Renown Score with each Horde or Alliance faction other than your starting faction reaches 10, increase your Renown Score with your starting faction by 2.
Revered. The first time your Renown Score with each Horde or Alliance faction other than your starting faction reaches 25, increase your Renown Score with your starting faction by 3.
Exalted. The first time your Renown Score with each Horde or Alliance faction other than your starting faction reaches 50, increase your Renown Score with your starting faction by 5.

options.label: Activate Rage
options.description:
While active, your Rage follows the rules below.

Damage Resistance. You have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

Rage Damage. When you make an attack using Strength—with either a weapon or an Unarmed Strike—and deal damage to the target, you gain a bonus to the damage that increases as you gain levels as a Barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian Features table.

Strength Advantage. You have Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.

No Concentration or Spells. You can’t maintain Concentration, and you can’t cast spells.

Duration. The Rage lasts until the end of your next turn, and it ends early if you don Heavy armor or have the Incapacitated condition. If your Rage is still active on your next turn, you can extend the Rage for another round by doing one of the following:

  • Make an attack roll against an enemy.
  • Force an enemy to make a saving throw.
  • Take a Bonus Action to extend your Rage.

Each time the Rage is extended, it lasts until the end of your next turn. You can maintain a Rage for up to 10 minutes.

Cleave. If you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using a Scythe, you can make a melee attack roll with the Scythe against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the Scythe’s damage, but don’t add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

options.label: Cleaver (Graze)

Graze. If your attack roll with a Cleaver misses a creature, you can deal damage to that creature equal to the ability modifier you used to make the attack roll. This damage is the same type dealt by the Cleaver, and the damage can be increased only by increasing the ability modifier.

options.label: Increase three scores (+1 / +1 / +1)
options.description: Increase your Strength, Constitution, and Wisdom by 1.

options.label: Increase two scores (+2 / +1)
options.description: Increase one of these scores by 2 and a different score by 1.

options.label: Acceptance
options.description:
Characteristics: Those who have gone through a deep and harrowing journey and came to face a truth so difficult that it hurt to accept it—and yet they did it anyways and eventually came to peace with that truth.

Boon Ability: When making a skill check you can choose to add a +5 bonus to the roll. Once you use this boon, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.label: Envy
options.description:
Characteristics: Someone whose insecurities or past trauma have driven them to desire what others have. This person covets something so much that they’d be willing to do anything to get it, even at the expense of their loved ones.

Boon Ability: Choose an ally creature that you can see and gain proficiency in a skill they have proficiency in. This effect lasts for 1 hour. While you have proficiency in the chosen skill, the ally you copied it from has disadvantage in all checks that use that skill.

options.label: Fearful
options.description:
Characteristics: Through one impactful moment or a slow build over time, this person has been stricken with a deep and overwhelming fear. This fear now clouds their judgment and overrides their emotions—it controls their life.

Boon Ability: If you are hit by an attack while an ally creature is within 5 feet of you, you can choose to have the ally take the damage instead of you. Once you use this boon, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.label: Forgiveness
options.description:
Characteristics: By accepting their emotions, this person can let go of their anger and frustrations, forgiving those who’ve wronged them and rekindling the damaged relationship.

Boon Ability: When you are hit by an attack, you can choose to cause all subsequent attacks made by the creature to be made at disadvantage. This effect lasts until the end of your next turn. Once you use this boon, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.label: Hate
options.description:
Characteristics: A person full of hate is blind to the effects their actions can have. To fulfill their vendetta they’re willing to alienate and even hurt those close to them.

Boon Ability: When you make an attack roll or skill check you can choose to change the roll to a 20. If you choose to do this all Charisma, Intelligence, and Wisdom checks are made at disadvantage for the next hour. Once you use this boon, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.label: Heroic
options.description:
Characteristics: A person who puts fear behind themselves and stands up in a time of need to the very best they can. Whether they fail or not they give everything they can to do what is right.

Boon Ability: When you would fail a Wisdom, Charisma, or Intelligence saving throw, you can instead choose to succeed. Once you use this boon, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.label: Mercy
options.description:
Characteristics: Those with the power to deal out judgment onto others but have the compassion and understanding to hold back.

Boon Ability: When you make an attack that would drop a creature below zero hit points, you can choose to forgo the damage, making a Charisma skill check with advantage instead. Once you use this boon, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.label: Shame
options.description:
Characteristics: Devastated by a mistake they’ve made or a circumstance forced on them, this person now hates a part of themselves. This thing feels as if it is out in the open for all to see, and they can’t stand the thought of others judging them for it.

Boon Ability: As a bonus action, all creatures within 60 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be unable to look in your direction until the end of your next turn. The DC for this boon is equal to 10 + your level. Once you use this boon, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.label: Selfishness
options.description:
Characteristics: Someone whose actions have worsened the lives of those closest to them. A character that, when they could have done the right thing, chose the path for the betterment of themselves over others.

Boon Ability: When you take damage, you can choose to regain 2 hit points for each ally you have within 30 feet of you. When you do so, each ally suffers a number of Necrotic damage equal to the hit points you recovered. Once you use this boon, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.label: Selfless
options.description:
Characteristics: Above all else, this person puts those around them before themselves. They wish to help the people they care the most about, sometimes to the detriment of their well-being.

Boon Ability: On your turn, you can forgo your action, allowing a character that can see or hear you to take an action or move. Once you use this boon, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.label: Bestial Awakening (Intelligence)
options.description:
The feral world calls to your soul, howling for you to join it. You can give in to the call and transform into a beast, but the touch of silver bites you more deeply than the sharpest fang.

Beast Skin. You always have the Polymorph spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot or spell components but can target only yourself, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast it using slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for the spell when you cast it without a spell slot.

Searing Silver. Damage from Silvered Weapons ignores any Resistance or Immunity to damage you have. If you take damage from a Silvered Weapon or touch silver with your bare skin (or its equivalent), you can’t regain Hit Points until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

options.label: Call of the Lonely
options.description:
In the depths of your solitude, and when your hope withered on the branch, you were granted a companion you can call on. You never have to be alone again. This companion is Friendly toward you but is deeply unsettling to your allies.

Never Alone. When no other creature can see you, you can use a Bonus Action to call your companion, which appears in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of you. It takes the form of a person or a vague silhouette, and it uses the Doppelganger stat block. It is Friendly toward you and acts as your ally, and it takes its turn on your Initiative in combat. It disappears after 1 hour, when it dies, when you die, or when you use an action to politely dismiss it. When it disappears, it drops anything it was wearing or carrying.

Once you use this Bonus Action, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Precocious Friend. The companion sometimes appears with trinkets, Cursed Curios*, or other items. It might tell you where it got them, or it might not (GM’s choice). If it took the object from someone who misses it or wants it back, that could create difficulties for you.

Unsettling Presence. While your companion is summoned, both it and you exude a frightful air that unnerves your allies. While the companion is summoned, a creature that isn’t Hostile toward you that starts its turn able to see you or the companion must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition until the start of its next turn.

options.label: Collector of Stories (Intelligence)
options.description:
You have an insatiable desire to gather the tales of the world. Sometimes, you inadvertently take the story of meeting another person and keep it to yourself, forever.

Gathered Tales. You always have the Legend Lore spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot or spell components, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast it using slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for the spell when you cast it without a spell slot.

Hoarded Stories. When you use this bargain to cast Legend Lore without a spell slot, a Friendly NPC (the GM chooses) forgets ever meeting you. You can meet them again and attempt to rebuild a relationship, but you forever cause an unsettling discomfort in them. That NPC’s attitude toward you can’t ever improve beyond Indifferent, and you have Disadvantage on all Charisma checks against them.

options.label: Crooked Fortune
options.description:
The crooked fate that governs Druskenvald has taken a liking to you. You can avoid calamity, but you must pay back your good fortune eventually.

Cheat Fate. When you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead. When you do so, if you would take half damage on a successful save, you take no damage instead. Once you use Cheat Fate, you can’t use it again until you pay the price (see below).

Delayed Price. After you use Cheat Fate, your next three saving throws have Disadvantage and can’t have Advantage, and you gain 1 Exhaustion level when you succeed on one of the saves. Once you succeed or fail on the third saving throw, you regain the use of Cheat Fate. The powers that govern the warp and weft of fate don’t take kindly to cheating outside their terms—at the GM’s discretion, saving throws made intentionally or without true consequences simply to pay this price painlessly don’t count.

options.label: Cult of Personality
options.description:
You are a force of charm and allure with which to be reckoned. While others fall over themselves to stumble into your good graces, you might find that you end up needing them more than they need you.

Honeyed Words. As a Magic action, you can speak sweet words to a creature within 60 feet of you. The creature has the Charmed condition for 24 hours, until you use this feature again, or until you or your allies deal any damage to the target or force it to make a saving throw. The Charmed target is your ally and follows your commands as long as they don’t require the target to harm itself. If the target carries out a command it finds odious, it makes a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw, ending the condition on itself on a success. Once the condition ends, the target is immune to this feature for 24 hours.

If the target has Immunity to the Charmed condition, it instead has Disadvantage on D20 Tests until the start of your next turn, and you gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to your level. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Solitary Weakness. If you start your turn with no allies that you can see or hear within 20 feet of you, you lose any Temporary Hit Points you have from any source, and you have Disadvantage on D20 Tests until the start of your next turn.

options.label: Hand of Death
options.description:
Death has no claim on you. In exchange for staying its cold hand without that hand closing, you become a maw through which death feeds on the world around you.

Adamant Endurance. You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws.

Cling to Life. When you have 0 Hit Points at the start of your turn, or when you die, you can instead choose to regain a number of Hit Points equal to half your maximum. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again. After using it, whenever you regain Hit Points through any means, you gain only half that amount. Once a Humanoid (other than you) dies within 30 feet of you, you regain the use of this feature, and you can regain Hit Points as normal.

Death Knell. Other creatures within 10 feet of you have Disadvantage on Death Saving Throws, and you can’t restore Hit Points to a creature with 0 Hit Points by any means.

options.label: Might of the Old
options.description:
Ancient and primeval power dwells within the oldest forests of Druskenvald. These powers pour their strength into you but can overwhelm you with their unchanging nature.

Ancient Might. Your Strength score increases by 2, to a maximum of 22, and your Dexterity score decreases by 2.

Primeval Strength. As a Bonus Action, you can call upon the might of the ancients to raise your Strength score to 25 for 1 minute, during which time you deal double damage to objects. Once you use this Bonus Action, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Pyre’s Price. When you activate Primeval Strength, your skin takes on a bark-like texture, during which time you have Vulnerability to Fire damage. Your skin returns to normal when you finish a Long Rest.

options.label: Self-Serving Sacrifice (Intelligence)
options.description:
You can snatch others from the jaws of death, but your own grip lingers too tightly. The feeling of saving others from suffering fills you with resolve, even as it drains the vigor from those you rescue.

Critical Savior. When a creature within 120 feet of you is subjected to a Critical Hit or is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can use your Reaction to magically switch places with the target. Each of you teleports to the other’s space. Roll a number of d6s equal to half your level. You take Force damage equal to the total rolled, you gain Heroic Inspiration, and your Exhaustion level, if any, is reduced by 1. The target regains Hit Points equal to the total rolled and gains 1 Exhaustion level. You can’t use this feature again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Draining Presence. When you finish a Short or Long Rest, each creature within 100 feet of you loses one Hit Point Die (before spending Hit Dice in the case of finishing a Short Rest).

Final Sacrifice. You can cast True Resurrection using this bargain requiring no spell slot or spell components. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for the spell when you cast it without a spell slot.

When you cast the spell this way, you die, and nothing can prevent it. Your soul is bound to torment the creature you returned to life, and you can’t be raised from the dead by any means. When the creature takes a Long Rest, it must roll a d20 halfway through the rest’s duration. On a 1, your soul takes the form of a Wraith within 100 feet of the creature and tries to kill it. The wraith vanishes after 8 hours, or when it dies. Once the wraith appears, it can’t appear again for 30 days.

options.label: Shrouded Spirit
options.description:
The pall of death drapes over you like the Shroud of Druskenvald. This shroud protects you from the depredations of the Undead, but it draws you ever nearer to their cold embrace.

Inured to Undeath. You have Resistance to Necrotic damage, and you have Advantage on saving throws against spells and effects created by Undead.

Unholy Appetite. You must consume one pound of raw flesh (it needn’t be fresh) per day or suffer Malnutrition.

Withering Soul. Features that detect your creature type, such as a Paladin’s Divine Sense or the Detect Evil and Good spell, treat you as Undead if your creature type isn’t Undead already.

options.label: Skin of Coffin Nails
options.description:
Your body becomes as coldly unrelenting as iron nails sealing away the dead. You can shrug off staggering punishment, but the waters of the world no longer embrace you, as if spiting your defiance.

Iron Grit. You gain Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage (your choice when you select this Dark Bargain). You can change the damage type to one of the other options when you finish a Short or Long Rest. When you suffer a Critical Hit from the chosen damage type, it becomes a normal hit instead.

Watery Doom. When you are immersed in water or splashed with at least 1 gallon of water (such as from a bucket or being rained on), your skin tightens and grows rusty until you finish a Short or Long Rest. During that time, your Speed and the time you can hold your breath are halved, and your Resistance to the chosen damage type for Iron Grit becomes Vulnerability instead. At the GM’s discretion, other liquids can also trigger this feature.

options.label: Stilled Hungers
options.description:
Food, drink, and maladies of the flesh have lost their hold over you, but these are the very things that keep a soul vital while in the land of the living. Your mind grows ravenous absent those urges—your thoughts crack with gnawing fears, and your dreams wither into crooked nightmares.

Sated Cravings. Forgoing food and drink doesn’t give you Exhaustion levels. You have Resistance to Poison damage, and you have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Poisoned condition.

Tenuous Psyche. You have Vulnerability to Psychic damage and Disadvantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Frightened condition. A Calm Emotions spell cast on you suppresses this feature for its duration.

options.label: Unquenchable Fury
options.description:
Anger is a powerful tool. This bargain stokes it into a formidable inferno, but it threatens to consume everything in its path.

Furious Onslaught. As a Bonus Action, or when you take the Attack action on your turn, you can choose to enter a fury. While in this fury, you can make one additional melee attack when you take the Attack action on your turn, and you reduce all damage you take by an amount equal to your Proficiency Bonus. The fury ends if you have the Incapacitated condition, if you die, or if you end your turn and there are no creatures within 60 feet of you that you can see or hear. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You also regain the use of this feature when you kill a Humanoid.

Red Haze. While you are in a fury, you must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw at the start of each of your turns. On a successful save, you can choose to end your fury or continue it. On a failed save, you no longer make the saving throw at the start of your turns, and you regard the creature nearest to you that you can see or hear as your enemy (if there are multiple, choose one at random). options.description:

Murderous Flight. As a Bonus Action, you can magically gain a Fly Speed equal to your Speed (and you can hover) for 10 minutes. During this time, a mass of shadows takes the shape of a murder of crows and ravens (but they aren’t truly creatures). The birds appear in a 20-foot Emanation originating from you and take flight and whirl around you when you fly. Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest, unless you gain 1 Exhaustion level to use it again early.

While the birds are present, you have Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, and the birds whisper your secrets into the minds of other creatures, granting them Advantage on Wisdom (Insight or Perception) checks made against you.

You have been wronged. Now your fate is painted with blood.

Among the Northlanders, no oath is more serious than an oath of vengeance. But when justice cannot be achieved by any other means, a sworn promise to mete out revenge for wrongdoing is the only answer that remains. Those who make such oaths are called Bloodsworn, and their vengeance becomes a tale told by skalds for generations.

As a Bloodsworn, your ultimate goal is revenge upon the one (or ones) who wronged you. Unfortunately, the wrongdoer is beyond your reach, at least for now. This means your plan must be carried out over weeks, months, or even longer. During this time, you’ll no doubt be distracted by other adventures, but your focus demands that you always return to your oath. Bloodsworn must have been wronged or harmed in some way before the gods will accept their blood oath. In most cases, your vengeance will be fatal to your target, but in some situations, other punishments may be more fitting, especially if the wrong you’re avenging doesn’t itself involve a death.

4 The power-mad jarl of our lands has destroyed my community. I have a cunning plan to ensure he is overthrown.
5 My trusted shieldmate betrayed me and left me to die. Now I shall return the favor.
6 I was shamed by the false words of another. I will deliver vengeance tenfold upon my accuser.

You bear the brunt of a curse of ill luck, and it’ll get worse before the end.

Northlanders place great faith in the existence of luck. The gods can bestow good fortune upon the faithful, and honorable actions can directly lead to successful endeavors. Likewise, disreputable behavior can bring failure not only to you, but to future generations of your family.

You are one of the unfortunates, chosen by fate or the gods to suffer from ill luck wherever you go. Perhaps you earned this curse through dishonor, oathbreaking, or cowardice. You might bear misfortune as a virtual heirloom, passed down to you by a disreputable ancestor. Other cursemarked are victims of witch’s curses or similar supernatural effects. Whatever the reason, you can’t seem to catch a break.

Strangely, the presence of a Cursemarked can often bring good fortune to those nearby. As long as your friends are willing to put up with your occasional mishaps, the long-term benefit might well be worthwhile. Meanwhile, however, the cursemarked searches for some way to atone for their misdeeds, real or imagined, knowing such a road will be long and will certainly grow worse before the end. 2 I can only lift this curse by clearing the name of an ancestor falsely accused of murder.
3 I must prove my courage to the gods by defeating a tribe of marauding giants.
4 I will invoke Freyr’s blessing by forging peace between two warring clans.
5 To end this curse, I shall endure trials of my honor, my valor, and my selflessness.
6 I must convince Wotan himself to intervene and convince the Norns to reshape my fate.

The milestone features described below trigger when you roll for specific mechanics (saving throws, ability checks or attack roll, depending on the feature) and get a result within the range of numbers indicated in the bracket for each milestone. Glory lies just over the horizon. Time to find it.

Explorers occupy an unusual place in Northlands society. Though revered for their courage, they rarely find a comfortable place in a community. Driven by wanderlust, curiosity, boredom, or a simple inability to relate to civilized folks, the Explorer spends most of their time in the wilderness. Some climb mountains, others set sail for lost lands, and still others delve through dark tunnels beneath the earth. For an Explorer, the greatest treasure awaits beyond the next hill.

Whether by choice or by fate, you follow the path less traveled. Perhaps you’re a rugged seafarer or mountaineer seeking discoveries in the wild. Other Explorers are treasure hunters, royal mapmakers, or seekers of truth. You might be an exile, outlaw, or iconoclast, who simply can’t get along with others. Or you might be driven by vision or prophecy to forsake hearth and home for the unknown.

GM Note. This thread brings flavorful Northlands themes into a campaign and can be taken up by characters of any class. However, it can tread on the toes of any Rangers in the party. Consult with your Ranger players before allowing a character to take on this thread to make sure no feelings will be hurt.

2 To avert Ragnarok, I must carry a prophecy to a far-flung land.
3 My mother died searching for the headwaters of the Tearstain River. I shall complete her quest.
4 I seek a sapling of the World Tree, rumored to be growing on a tiny island in the Nieder Strait.
5 Once I decipher the ancient map I hold, I’ll delve into the depths of Narvegr Maw.
6 The Frozen Palace of the last Hyperborean lies somewhere in the Bleak Expanse. I’ll find it and return with his icy crown.

When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain your choice of one the following benefits.

Dream Gift. A god, Norn, or other powerful being has given you a gift in a dream. When you awoke, you had a Common magic item of the GM’s choice that may aid you.

Your fate is written. Make it glorious.

Many warriors loudly boast of their desire for a noble death or an honorable end in battle, to thus earn a seat in the great hall of Valhalla. These boasts are but hopeful wishes since most individuals never see the path of their future. You, however, are not most individuals. You have been blessed, or perhaps cursed, with the knowledge of your end, though this knowledge doesn’t tell you if you succeed or fail in the circumstance surrounding your death. You might know you will die facing a dark warlord, but you don’t know if you will defeat her. Despite this, the Norns have given you a rare opportunity. The knowledge you possess will help you ensure your death is worthy of the sagas.

Some of those who are Fatebound are marked from birth. Others learn of their fate from seers, shamans, or divine visions. Some heroes earn this thread after engaging in activities that move the gods or the Norns to reward them with such a potent end.

Fatebound and Death. Keep in mind that having this thread may mean you can’t die before your fated time, but it doesn’t mean you will reach that point whole and healthy. While your fate is inevitable, luck alone determines your condition when you meet that end. Do you lead a glorious charge across the battlefield? Or are you left guarding the baggage? Has every confrontation leading up to your end prepared you to defeat your ultimate foe? Or has a lifetime of avoidance left you ill-prepared?

If a Fatebound PC is killed before their time, and magical resurrection is not an option, a GM could instead choose for them to be injured in a significant way—such as the loss of a limb or eye. These injuries should not be able to be healed without high-level magic. Alternatively, perhaps they lose one of their powerful magical items instead of their lives, or they might suffer a level of Exhaustion until they reach their next milestone. The GM and player should agree on this complication.

GM Note: The Fatebound is an unusual thread in that its final milestone specifically describes the manner in which a character might meet with a permanent death, likely as part of the final accomplishment of their goal, and then empowers the PCs’ allies as a reward. Most importantly, this thread should be something the player consciously selects.

3 To defend my people from invasion, I pledge to pay any price, including my own life.
4 I shall search for and find a fabled lost treasure, but I will die in the process.
5 I will rise to become the North’s greatest reaver, then perish battling the World Serpent.
6 I seek the truth behind the fall of Nordheim, though it will cost my life to learn it.

options.label: Herald (Level 1)
options.description:
Least Milestone Feature

When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain the following benefits.

Storyteller’s Knack. You learn three languages of your choice.

Performer’s Reward. If you have at least 3 days of downtime between adventures, you can earn GP equal to 10 times your character level by performing your stories in taverns, on the street, or for powerful patrons. Additional downtime events don’t increase this reward.

Your stories don’t just recount events . . . they shape history.

Storytellers are revered in the Northlands. Whether a skald sharing tales around a fire, a lore keeper gathering sagas to pass down the generations, or a grizzled reaver frightening young warriors by recalling harrowing battles, the tradition of collecting stories is respected across nearly all cultures in the region. As a Herald, you are a proud, if temporary, part of this tradition, driven by a need to spread stories during your travels to accomplish a specific end.

Perhaps your stories encourage downtrodden karls to rise up against their cruel jarl, warn a region about an approaching invasion, or convince warriors to join your cause. Part skald, part herald, part envoy, you will use your tales and stories to sway the minds of your audience and help shape the world.

Goals. Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Herald Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

GM Note. This thread brings flavorful Northlands themes into a campaign and can be taken up by characters of any class. However, it can tread on the toes of any Bards in the party. Consult with your Bard players before allowing a character to take on this thread to make sure no feelings will be hurt.

Herald Goals
d6 Goal
1 The feared invasion from Jotunheim approaches, and the country must be warned.
2 By telling the sagas, I will gather support for the greatest raid the North has ever launched.
3 My tales flatter Thor and Wotan in the hope they will support our struggle against the forces of Chernobog and Angrboda.
4 I spread the word of the great crusade to eradicate the darkness beneath Tanserhall. Heed my call!
5 I seek a lost treasure of Hyperborea, and by spreading tales of similar treasures, I hope to find a path to a hidden vault.
6 To rouse the people against their evil king, I shall assemble an array of sorrowful tales of corruption that cannot be ignored.

Least Milestone Feature

When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain the following benefit.

Predator’s Mark. You have Advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks made to track creatures, and on a failed check it only takes you half the time to reacquire the tracks (5 minutes in a confined area, or half an hour outdoors).

Neither storm nor night nor bloody fang shall slow your relentless pursuit.

Hunting is as old as the Northlands itself. From volcanic peaks to frigid fens and aurora-bathed glaciers, the tales of hunters are sung alongside those of heroes and gods. While some may hunt for survival or vengeance, you are different. You are a hunter to be feared, as you hunt for the thrill of the chase and the glory of victory.

As a Legend Hunter, you may have been chosen by the Norns, blessed by a god, or forged in trials of blood and grift. No matter how you come to it, your extraordinary search for greater and greater prey sets you apart from those who hunt merely for survival. You do not merely forge trails; you craft sagas. You do not merely slay beasts; you end legends to become a legend.

Goals. Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Legend Hunter Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

Legend Hunter Goals
d6 Goal
1 I will prove my valor by tracking down and slaying a legendary monster that has been destroying villages.
2 I hunt for a mythical two-headed jotun somewhere in the Bleak Expanse.
3 Besting a great dragon in its lair shall be my ultimate victory.
4 I will go beneath the waves to bring low the mother of all krakens.
5 I will bring back the head of Fenris.
6 My legend will be assured when I go among the roots of Yggdrasil to slay Nidhogg.

options.label: Sworn Huskarl (Level 1)
options.description:
Least Milestone Feature

When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain the following benefit.

Jarl’s Authority. The authority granted you by your loyal service can sway the opinions of others. Before rolling an Intimidation or Persuasion check to influence someone who knows and respects (or fears) your ruler, you can choose to treat the d20 roll as if you’d rolled a natural 15. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

You carry out the will of your king, no matter the risk.

You have pledged your loyalty to an important personage, promising to guard them or travel across the Northlands in their service, risking danger as you seek to accomplish a great task. In the past, it was expected that a huskarl would swear to serve a lord for life or until they were dismissed. While jarls still take huskarls in that way, they also accept the service of huskarls on a temporary basis, to perform specific deeds or until certain threats are dealt with. These are the types of huskarls described in this thread.

The sworn huskarl enjoys a position of respect within their lord’s retinue. More than a mere bodyguard, you are a trusted agent acting on your ruler’s behalf. You carry some of their authority with you, but that also comes with the responsibility to act in ways they would approve. Sworn huskarls who bring shame to their jarl don’t remain in service for long.

A jarl takes on a new huskarl with a simple ceremony in which the huskarl swears an oath in the longhouse before a gathering of other members of the felag. During the oath-swearing, the goals or timeframe for the service are mentioned (unless the jarl keeps your mission a secret). Traditionally, your reasons for serving are respect for the lord, payment, or power. However, in some cases your oath may hold a secret. Perhaps you made it under threat of violence or under false pretenses. Or maybe your lord doesn’t deserve such loyalty. You might serve under protest or with your own goal that’s unknown to your ruler.

Goals. Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Sworn Huskarl Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

Sworn Huskarl Goals
d6 Goal
1 I will find my king’s long-lost child so that my kingdom will have a true heir.
2 My queen depends on me to find and slay the pretender who claims a blood right to her throne.
3 I must root out a hidden sect of the Cult of Ragnarok that grows within my jarl’s land.
4 Giant raiding parties threaten the land. My jarl calls upon me to destroy them and make the land safe once more.
5 I can only earn my freedom by finding the stolen crown of my sadistic monarch.
6 I serve only until I can discover a way to overthrow this corrupt king, who took the throne through dark sorcery.

Your faction is the Alliance.

The peoples of the Alliance are bound together by proud traditions of nobility, honor, faith, justice, and sacrifice. The disparate cultures that make up this faction contribute technical, arcane, and spiritual wisdom toward the goal of a peaceful and just world. The highest ideals of the Alliance are tradition, justice, and duty, matching closely to the Lawful Good alignment.

The Alliance is a military coalition whose leadership is dependent on the unified will of its member peoples. By default, the high king (or other leader) of Stormwind has served as commander of the Alliance, but the commander has authority over only the military forces that other Alliance leaders commit to the Alliance’s cause. Thus, in practice, the human king leads as part of a council made up of all the Alliance leaders.

options.label: Horde
options.description:
Your faction is the Horde.

The proud nations of the Horde are loosely joined in an alliance of convenience against a hostile world that would see them destroyed. Focused and ferocious, the Horde values strength and honor but struggles to keep its members’ aggression in check. The Horde’s ideals are unity, freedom, and hope, matching closely to the Chaotic Good alignment.

From the time of its founding until the end of the Fourth War, the Horde was led by a single warchief. The orc shaman Thrall held that position from before the Third War until he stepped down to join the Earthen Ring (described later in this chapter) during the Cataclysm. He was succeeded by the warmongering Garrosh Hellscream, who was in turn deposed by a combination of Alliance pressure and a rebellion of the Darkspear trolls. The troll chieftain Vol’jin then took up the mantle, becoming the first non-orc to hold the title, but Vol’jin died during the Burning Legion’s third invasion of Azeroth. The undead high elf Sylvanas Windrunner then became warchief, but she ultimately abandoned the Horde to pursue her own agenda. Since her departure, a Horde Council made up of the leaders of the Horde’s subfactions has governed the Horde.

The Earthen Ring is a gathering of Azeroth’s most powerful shaman, working together to preserve the balance among the elements. The members of the Earthen Ring oppose destructive forces such as the Twilight’s Hammer cult, the rampaging black dragon Deathwing, and the Burning Legion, and they work tirelessly to heal the wounds inflicted on Azeroth by such forces. Insisting on a neutral stance in mortal conflicts (and a generally Neutral alignment), the Earthen Ring welcomes members from both the Alliance and the Horde, though the peoples of the Alliance— particularly draenei, Wildhammer dwarves, and humans of Kul Tiras—are recent additions to the organization. It also includes murlocs, the Krokul draenei, and other druids who haven’t chosen a side in the Alliance–Horde conflict.

The Earthen Ring is governed by the Elder Council, which gathers at a shrine perched at the edge of the Maelstrom called the Heart of Azeroth. The order also maintains a ritual circle just outside Stormwind’s walls (the Eastern Earthshrine) and another above Orgrimmar (the Western Earthshrine). Affiliated with the Alliance and the Horde respectively, the Explorers’ League and the Reliquary are scholarly organizations dedicated to the practice of archaeology and the study of history, seeking to understand the origins of life and culture on Azeroth.

Magni Bronzebeard, the king of Ironforge, founded the Explorers’ League by decree after dwarf-led expeditions uncovered surprising facts about the dwarves’ connection to the ancient titans. Declaring that learning this history was more important than mining and engineering, Magni directed the Explorers’ League to focus on archaeological work and plumbing the secrets of the ancient world. The league quickly expanded its scope to encompass natural history as well as the history of all Azeroth’s peoples, and it soon accepted citizens of other Alliance nations as members. High Explorer Muninn Magellas is the leader of the Explorers’ League, and the organization’s headquarters remains in Ironforge, in the Hall of Explorers.

The Reliquary, in contrast, began as an effort to harness the power of ancient relics for the benefit of the blood elves and their allies in the Horde. The leader and founder of the Reliquary, Tae’thelan Bloodwatcher, believed such artifacts should be carefully studied, not feared. Tae’thelan’s ultimate goal in founding the Reliquary was to free the blood elves from their magical addiction and reunite them. When the blood elves joined the Horde, the Reliquary opened its membership to all members of the Horde, but its headquarters (also called the Reliquary) remains in Silvermoon City.

Relic Rivals

Despite their different origins (and different alignments, corresponding to the difference between the Alliance and the Horde), the Explorers’ League and the Reliquary use similar methods and often vie for access to the same sites. For most of recent history, the organizations were bitter rivals, with the tension between them often erupting into violent conflict. During this time, the factions are mutually hostile (see “Mutually Hostile Factions”).

However, with the reemergence of the Dragon Isles and the subsequent discovery of Khaz Algar, the two organizations have set aside their old rivalry and formed joint expeditions. During this period, a character’s Renown Score with either faction applies to both factions, so having a Renown Score of 3+ with either one makes members of both factions Friendly by default.

Mutually Hostile Factions

World of Warcraft features many opposing factions that are so hostile to each other that any renown gain with one faction automatically results in a loss of renown with the other. The Explorers’ League and the Reliquary were mutually hostile before they were forced to cooperate in exploring the Dragon Isles. Other examples include the Scryers and the Aldor of Shattrath City, as well as the Frenzyheart Tribe of wolvar and the gorlock Oracles of Sholazar Basin. In situations like these, a character’s Renown Score with a faction can drop below 0, which means members of that faction are Hostile to the character by default.

The Kirin Tor began as a secretive mages’ guild within the Empire of Arathor, the first great human civilization of the Eastern Kingdoms. Viewed with suspicion by much of the populace, the mages of Arathor secluded themselves in their own city, Dalaran, which became a beacon to mages from across Azeroth. With the fall of Arathor, Dalaran became a nation in its own right, one of Arathor’s seven successor kingdoms, and the Council of Six who led the Kirin Tor became the rulers of this city-state. Razed during the Third War, Dalaran was rebuilt behind powerful warding spells and later transformed into a flying island that could be relocated to safety when needed. From its original site in the Hillsbrad Foothills, Dalaran moved first to Northrend’s Crystalsong Forest, then above Karazhan in Deadwind Pass, then to the Broken Isles, then above the Isle of Dorn in Khaz Algar. There it met its doom at the hands of Xal’atath’s forces of the Void, but the survivors of the Kirin Tor remain in Dornogal, coordinating the magical defense of Azeroth.

The Council of Six, the leadership of the Kirin Tor, is made up of the most senior members of the Kirin Tor. Its leaders have included Archmage Rhonin, who oversaw the rebuilding of Dalaran after the Third War, Lady Jaina Proudmoore, and Archmage Khadgar, who was imprisoned by Xal’atath just before Dalaran’s destruction. The Steamwheedle Cartel is one of the largest and richest goblin cartels, having maintained a careful neutrality in the conflict between the Alliance and the Horde since the Second War (and a generally Neutral alignment). From its headquarters in Gadgetzan (in Tanaris), the cartel oversees operations across Azeroth and even Outland. It also runs Booty Bay (in Stranglethorn), Ratchet (in the Northern Barrens), and Everlook (in Winterspring), as well as smaller outposts. The cartel’s hands are in virtually every line of work, with a specialty in premium- grade alchemy (at least since the alchemist Marin Noggenfogger assumed the position of trade prince). Besides potions, the cartel also deals in fuels, poisons, and industrial chemicals—what some goblins describe as “liquid assets.”

The Valdrakken Accord is the unified might of all dragonkind, seeking to protect not only the Dragon Isles but all of Azeroth according to the ancient charge given to the five Dragon Aspects (see chapter 6). The accord has also expanded its mission to include dragons beyond the five flights—in particular those who follow Vyranoth, who has been empowered as the Aspect of Storms.

The mission of the Dragon Aspects means that what is good for dragonkind is generally beneficial for all of Azeroth. The dragons oppose the Burning Legion, the lingering forces of the Old Gods and elementals they have corrupted, the remnants of the Scourge, the powers of the Void, and any other force that might threaten Azeroth and its inhabitants. That said, working with the dragons means viewing the world’s conflicts from their perspective (which is generally Neutral) and solving problems their way.

The leaders of the Valdrakken Accord are the six Dragon Aspects: Alexstrasza, Nozdormu, Kalecgos, Merithra, Ebyssian, and Vyranoth. Their base of operations is the city of Valdrakken in the Dragon Isles.

The leader of the faction is High Chieftain Baine Bloodhoof, who succeeded his father, Cairne Bloodhoof, when Cairne died in an ill-fated duel against Garrosh Hellscream.

While your Bastion is in Thunder Bluff or elsewhere in Mulgore or Highmountain, your Renown Score with Thunder Bluff increases by 1.

options.label: Thunder Bluff: Honored
options.description:
Thunder Bluff: Honored

Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with Thunder Bluff

When you succeed on a check to gather herbs using herbalism (see chapter 3), you gain one extra resource, and you find a rare resource if you beat the check DC by 4 or more.

You can purchase equipment found in the Player’s Handbook, as well as Common or Uncommon magic items, from merchants of the faction at a 10% discount.

Thunder Bluff: Friendly

Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with Thunder Bluff

You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn Taurahe or gain proficiency with the Herbalism Kit.

Other members of the faction are Friendly to you by default.

options.label: Thunder Bluff: Revered
options.description:
Thunder Bluff: Revered

Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with Thunder Bluff

You can request the Charm of An’she from the leaders of Thunder Bluff before you undertake a quest on their behalf. This Charm allows you to cast Summon Beast (level 3 version). Once used three times, the Charm vanishes from you; it also vanishes if you complete or abandon the quest. Once you request a Charm, you can’t do so again until your Renown Score with Thunder Bluff increases.

Your faction discount increases to 15% and extends to Rare magic items.

You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn the Forsaken language or gain proficiency with Alchemist’s Supplies (see “Training”).

Training

Several renown perks give you the opportunity to work with a trainer to learn a language or gain a proficiency. The days required needn’t be consecutive, but you must spend 8 consecutive hours with the trainer for a day to count. You can gain only one tool proficiency from each renown perk.

Undercity Renown Perks

The Undercity faction encompasses the Forsaken aligned with the Horde. The faction was long led by Sylvanas Windrunner, who originally led the Forsaken who broke free from the control of the Lich King. When Sylvanas stepped into the leadership of the Horde as warchief, the Desolate Council was formed to govern the Forsaken in her place. The council, based now in the Ruins of Lordaeron, is made up of five leaders: Calia Menethil, Lilian Voss, Master Apothecary Faranell, Deathstalker Commander Belmont, and Dark Ranger Velonara.

While your Bastion is in Undercity or the Ruins of Lordaeron, your Renown Score with Undercity increases by 1.

class.name: Rage (Enter)
class.description:
You can imbue yourself with a primal power called Rage, a force that grants you extraordinary might and resilience. You can enter it as a Bonus Action if you aren’t wearing Heavy armor.

You can enter your Rage the number of times shown for your Barbarian level in the Rages column of the Barbarian Features table. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

While active, your Rage follows the rules below.

Damage Resistance. You have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

Rage Damage. When you make an attack using Strength—with either a weapon or an Unarmed Strike—and deal damage to the target, you gain a bonus to the damage that increases as you gain levels as a Barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian Features table.

Strength Advantage. You have Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.

No Concentration or Spells. You can’t maintain Concentration, and you can’t cast spells.

Duration. The Rage lasts until the end of your next turn, and it ends early if you don Heavy armor or have the [condition]Incapacitated[/condition] condition. If your Rage is still active on your next turn, you can extend the Rage for another round by doing one of the following:

  • Make an attack roll against an enemy.
  • Force an enemy to make a saving throw.
  • Take a Bonus Action to extend your Rage.

Each time the Rage is extended, it lasts until the end of your next turn. You can maintain a Rage for up to 10 minutes.
class.snippet: You can enter Rage if you aren’t wearing Heavy Armor. You can use Rage {{limiteduse}} times per Long Rest, and regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest.

class.name: Warrior of the Gods: Expend Dice
class.description:
A divine entity helps ensure you can continue the fight. You have a pool of four d12s that you can spend to heal yourself. As a Bonus Action, you can expend dice from the pool, roll them, and regain a number of Hit Points equal to the roll’s total.

Your pool regains all expended dice when you finish a Long Rest.

The pool’s maximum number of dice increases by one when you reach Barbarian levels 6 (5 dice), 12 (6 dice), and 17 (7 dice).
class.snippet: You have a pool of {{scalevalue}} that you can spend to heal yourself. As a Bonus Action, you can expend dice from the pool by rolling them and regaining HP equal to the roll’s total. You regain all expended dice when you finish a Long Rest.

class.name: Plant Totem
class.description:
You can coalesce elemental spirits into a totem that aids you and your allies. As a Bonus Action, you can plant one of the totems below into the ground in an unoccupied space you can see within 10 feet of yourself.

A totem is a Small object that has AC 10 and 1 Hit Point and lasts for 1 minute, until it drops to 0 Hit Points, or until you use this feature again. At the end of each of your turns, the totem pulses with elemental energy that fills a 30-foot [rules]Emanation[/rules].

Earthbind Totem. Each enemy in the Emanation has its Speed reduced by 10 feet until the end of your next turn.

Primal Knowledge Totem. Each ally in the Emanation is empowered with nature’s focus until the end of your next turn. While empowered in this way, whenever the creature makes an ability check using one of the following skills, the creature can make it as a Strength check even if it normally uses a different ability: [skill]Acrobatics[/skill], [skill]Intimidation[/skill], [skill]Perception[/skill], [skill]Stealth[/skill], or [skill]Survival[/skill]. After you plant this totem, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of this totem by expending one use of your Rage (no action required).

Tremor Totem. Each ally in the Emanation has Immunity to the [condition]Charmed[/condition] and [condition]Frightened[/condition] conditions until the end of your next turn. If the creature was already Charmed or Frightened, those conditions are suppressed until the end of its next turn.

Wind Rush Totem. Each ally in the Emanation has its Speed increased by 10 feet until the end of your next turn.

feat.name: Heavy Weapon Mastery
feat.description: When you hit a creature with a weapon that has the [wprop]Heavy[/wprop] property as part of the Attack action on your turn, you can cause the weapon to deal extra damage to the target. The extra damage equals your Proficiency Bonus.

feat.name: Cleave (Halberd)
feat.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of Halberds:

Cleave. If you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using a Halberd, you can make a melee attack roll with the Halberd against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the Halberd’s damage, but don’t add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.
feat.snippet: Cleave. Once per turn, if you hit a creature with a melee attack using a Halberd, you can make another melee attack with it against a second creature within 5 ft. of the first that’s within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the Halberd’s damage, but without your ability modifier (unless the modifier is negative).

feat.name: Graze (Glaive)
feat.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of Glaives:

Graze. If your attack roll with a Glaive misses a creature, you can deal damage to that creature equal to the ability modifier you used to make the attack roll. This damage is the same type dealt by the Glaive, and the damage can be increased only by increasing the ability modifier.
feat.snippet: Graze. If your attack roll with a Glaive misses a creature, you can deal damage to it equal to the ability modifier used to make the attack. This damage is the same type dealt by the Glaive, and can only be increased by increasing the ability modifier.

feat.name: Topple (Bola)
feat.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of Bola:

Topple. If you hit a creature with a Bola, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the [condition]Prone[/condition] condition.
